summary: Kanawha County steel fire tower, about 90 ft, erected on Johnson Knob near Whittaker in 1929; the registry says it has been removed. No source found describes the site today.

facts.status_note: The registry says the tower has been removed; the county list marks it gone.
facts.design: steel fire tower about 90 feet tall with a log cabin for living quarters
facts.agency: West Virginia Game & Fish Commission (registry); the lookout history page's header names the West Virginia Division of Forestry

events.note: Erected by the Southern West Virginia Forest Fire Protective Association, per an October 25, 1929 newspaper report. The state game, fish and forestry commission supervised construction.
Registered September 16, 2008 with the Former Fire Lookout Sites register.

evidence.supports: a 90-foot steel tower with a log cabin, erected on Johnson Knob near Whittaker, later given to the state commission
evidence.quote: A 90 foot steel forest fire tower and log cabin living quarters, erected on Johnson Knob, near Whittaker, by the Southern West Virginia Forest Fire Protective Association has been given to the state game and forestry commission.

evidence.supports: the protective association paid for the tower and the state commission supervised construction
evidence.quote: The cost of erecting the tower was defrayed by the protective association, while construction work was supervised by the state game, fish and forestry commission.

evidence.supports: the newspaper report is dated October 25, 1929
the page header lists the West Virginia Division of Forestry
the registry says the tower has been removed
the registry names the West Virginia Game & Fish Commission as administrator
evidence.quote: Administered by West Virginia Game & Fish Commission

evidence.supports: the site is in Kanawha County
the county list marks the Johnson Knob tower gone
evidence.quote: Kanawha Johnson Knob 38.06630 -81.40231 Tower Gone FFLOS US 160, WV 10

evidence.supports: the Whittaker Station tower is the former Gauley Mountain tower, relocated in October 2009
evidence.quote: The former Gauley Mountain Fire Tower was relocated to the Whittaker Station area of Cass Scenic Railroad State Park in October 2009

evidence.supports: the relocated tower is accessible by train from Cass
evidence.quote: The Blaw-Knox tower is accessible by train from Cass.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The registry names the West Virginia Game & Fish Commission. The Forest Lookouts page header names the West Virginia Division of Forestry. The 1929 report names the state game, fish and forestry commission. The story gives the registry name and notes the header.

notes_for_editor: Only two pages describe this tower in any detail: a 1929 newspaper report quoted on Forest Lookouts, and the registry entry. Removal date and present-day condition were not found in any fetched source, so the story says so. No staffing, fire, or rental records were found. Two search snippets mentioned a 73-foot tower and a $1,500 appropriation; they came from pages I could not open, so the figures are not used. The brief's height_m of 27.4 matches the 90-foot figure in the 1929 report. Do not confuse with the Whittaker Station tower, a relocated former Gauley Mountain tower.
